findings.reason: one added case (`--dry-run`, neither flag, refused naming both) is the only measurement that makes the dry-run half of the deliverable falsifiable; without it that half can be omitted silently, and the suite still reads green.
findings.text: the sixth case shows only that a `--dry-run` brief dispatch given `--plan-link` is not refused; no case shows that a `--dry-run` brief dispatch given neither flag IS refused, so an implementation that refuses on the live path alone passes all six cases and all five controls while contradicting the deliverable's claim that the refusal "covers both the live call and its `--dry-run` branch (near line 1917)"

findings.reason: one sentence fixing the placement ("above the pair split", or pair dispatch scoped out with its reason) decides whether that path is refused at dispatch; it changes no write path and no test file.
findings.text: the coverage sentence names only the live call and the `--dry-run` branch, but `crew dispatch` splits earlier at `if pair_backend:` (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1821`) and returns after `dispatch_pair`, whose two arms each call `plan_dispatch` directly with the same brief-bearing node (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1177` and `:1233`, neither gated on a plan link); the only placement that covers both described paths — before the `if dry_run:` split at `:1898`, which is after the pair branch — leaves an implement-role brief pair dispatch unrefused, so it is still first asked at landing, which is the defect s3 exists to remove
